page: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-4 is a graphics-optimized virtual machine featuring an Intel Xeon x86_64 CPU with 4 dedicated vCPUs, 2 physical cores, and 2 threads per core running at 2.2 GHz. The processor includes a 38 MB L3 cache and supports instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB per core. It features a bundled NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, which provides 24 GB of dedicated VRAM. This instance does not include local NVMe storage.

Performance benchmarks reveal a stark contrast between the host CPU and the accelerated GPU capabilities. Standard CPU-bound operations, including stress-ng, Geekbench, and Passmark CPU tests, consistently rank in the bottom 25%, indicating weak general-purpose compute performance. Memory bandwidth and single-threaded compression tasks also score in the lower percentiles. Conversely, the integrated NVIDIA L4 GPU delivers top-tier performance in machine learning workloads. Benchmark results for LLM inference using both small (135M) and medium (7B) models place this instance in the top 10% for prompt processing and text generation speeds.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the g2-standard-4 offers a specialized hardware profile where resource allocation is heavily weighted toward GPU acceleration rather than raw CPU power or high memory density. This makes it a highly cost-effective option for workloads that can offload execution to the GPU, such as low-to-medium scale LLM inference, graphics rendering, and AI model deployment. However, it is poorly suited for CPU-intensive tasks, database operations, or workloads requiring high local storage throughput due to the absence of local disks and the lower-performing host processor.
description: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-4 is a graphics-optimized instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor running at 2.2 GHz, 16.0 GB of system memory, and a single NVIDIA L4 GPU with 24 GB of VRAM. It does not include local storage. Benchmark data highlights a significant performance divergence: while standard CPU, memory bandwidth, and compression tests score in the bottom 25%, the GPU-accelerated LLM inference capabilities for small and medium models rank in the top 10% for both prompt processing and text generation. This hardware profile represents a qualitative tradeoff, offering cost-efficient GPU acceleration paired with modest host CPU resources. It is highly suited for machine learning inference, graphics rendering, and AI-driven applications, but is less effective for general-purpose compute or database workloads that rely heavily on high-performance host CPUs and local storage.
